circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281-kilometre track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for the Formula One season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that loops around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support categories. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence, qualifying it for the highest standard of international motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods, first from 1970 to 1987 under its original name, and then again from 1997 to 2003 following its reconstruction and shortening. The track underwent significant modifications between these eras before eventually adopting its current identity as a premier motorsport facility.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along Baku Boulevard, that spans 6. 003 kilometers, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit stretches 5. 412 km and has served as the venue for numerous racing categories including the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which marked the sport's inaugural Middle Eastern event. The track, holding a FIA Grade 1 license and featuring multiple configurations, has also hosted various racing series such as GP2, Australian V8 Supercars, and endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it versatile for various racing conditions. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a staple of motorsport since hosting the first Grand Prix in 1925. The venue serves as the home of Formula One's Belgian Grand Prix, which was part of the inaugural F1 season in 1950 and has been held annually since 1985, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its use in elite single-seater racing, the venue has hosted numerous other prominent motorsporting series including international sports car championships and North American open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019 before resuming in 2024, alongside newly introduced electric racing events.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this famous circuit became the venue for the inaugural 1948 British Grand Prix and hosted the first-ever Formula One World Championship race two years later. After decades of sharing the British Grand Prix with rival circuits, Silverstone secured the event permanently from 1987 onwards and continues to be the primary home of Britain's Formula One race.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, situated near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the sport's inaugural Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, faster than any other Formula One venue at the time, the track was constructed outside the city near a major highway rather than as a street circuit in Budapest's central park as originally planned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue, nicknamed "the Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and rapid corners, has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, apart from a 1980 closure for renovation work.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, with a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is internationally recognised as a premier Formula One racing destination and also hosts the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard. The track weaves past iconic venues and resorts including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of the most visually distinctive racing venues in the sport.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix on multiple occasions, with the most recent tenure beginning in 2015 following previous hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed specifically for Formula One by specialist track engineers, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 as the home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, winding around Monaco's harbor. Though officially known as the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely referred to by the name "Monte Carlo" since the majority of the track runs through that specific district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort spans 4. 259 kilometers and welcomed Formula One back to its schedule in 2021 with the restoration of the Dutch Grand Prix. The partnership between the circuit and Formula One will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometre FIA Grade 1 facility featuring a 1. 068-kilometre main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km motorsport venue in São Paulo, Brazil, that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track also features a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along the Red Sea waterfront in Saudi Arabia, serving as the host track for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since its debut in 2021, while also accommodating Formula E racing from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront area, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a versatile design combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major motorsport events including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, alongside various other racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai nationality.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships during his 23-season career while claiming 32 race victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24-hour victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One drivers' title and the world endurance drivers' crown.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed six grand prix victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One for the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his previous tenure at Mercedes where he secured two consecutive runner-up finishes in the championship standings. Across his 13-year career in the sport, he has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto, an Argentine motorsport competitor, currently drives for Alpine in the Formula One championship.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines prototype racing in the European Le Mans Series with his reserve driver responsibilities at Haas. He made limited Formula One appearances across seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The highlight of his career came in 2020 when he secured victory at the Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: A Franco-Algerian driver representing France, Isack Alexandre Hadjar currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple racing records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved success in endurance racing by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a racing driver from New Zealand currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who has competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he races for BMW in the World Endurance Championship with WRT and drives part-time in NASCAR's top series for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver competing for McLaren who secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship title with the team. Across his eight-season career, he has claimed victory in 11 Grand Prix races.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for Haas. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory in 2021 while driving for Alpine, winning the Hungarian round of the championship.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. The two-time Grand Prix winner finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull, establishing himself as a competitive force in the series.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian motorsport talent, currently drives for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons competing in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams after a successful career spanning 12 seasons, during which he has secured four Grand Prix victories.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. His Formula One career spanned 2023 to 2024, after which he transitioned to sports car racing, including previous competition in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda has participated in Formula One spanning from 2021 through 2025, currently holding a reserve driver position across Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen is a Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing who has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season Formula One career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently serving as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the championship between 2022 and 2024, making him the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, following Renault's rebranding of its works outfit to promote its sports car marque. Operating under a French licence and powered by Mercedes engines, Alpine secured its only victory during this era when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has engaged in Formula One competition through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating under AMR GP Limited as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, fielding cars continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially called "the Prancing Horse" after its iconic emblem, remains synonymous with the sport's history and achievement.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed F1 team in 2014, with the squad entering the championship for the first time in 2016. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner who held the position since the team's establishment before departing in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss engineering firm Sauber Motorsport, established in 1970, competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent constructor while achieving notable success in endurance racing, including a Le Mans victory with Mercedes-Benz. The team departed the championship in 2025 after becoming the fourth-longest-running constructor by race entries, with its operations subsequently acquired by Audi to establish their factory F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its technology facility in Woking, operating as part of the wider McLaren Group infrastructure. The team functions as a subsidiary under the ownership of Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 in both managerial and technical capacities, with its current racing operation based in Brackley under a German licence. The team, officially competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, restructured its ownership in 2022 to include equal stakes held by the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The squad is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" within racing circles.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the energy drink conglomerate's second constructor entry on the grid.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team strategy, alongside the flagship Red Bull Racing operation. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as the second constructor under the Austrian energy drink conglomerate's ownership structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed outfit headquartered in England, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its establishment in 2005 under Christian Horner's long-standing stewardship. The team is part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team motorsport portfolio, with the squad transitioning to new leadership under Laurent Mekies in 2025 following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, evolved from Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
